entries.hunt_notes: Constructeur britannique (1957) d'amplis ET de guitares (Phantom, Teardrop/Mark VI). Guitares des années 1960 faites au Royaume-Uni puis, dès 1965, chez EKO (Italie) ; certains modèles chez Matsumoku (Japon).

sources.title: Vox (musical equipment)
sources.excerpt: originally made in England but soon after made by EKO of Italy … produced in Japan, where the Standard & Custom 24 & 25 guitars and basses were built by Matsumoku

sources.title: Vox Mark VI Teardrop Guitar V222
sources.excerpt: by 1965, the popularity and world wide demand for Vox guitars caused JMI to supplement UK production at Eko in Italy.

entries.hunt_notes: Marque américaine (1935), gamme économique de National puis de Valco : guitares électriques (Ozark, Dual Tone…), basses et amplis. Inactive après la faillite de Valco, relancée en 2014.

sources.title: Supro
sources.excerpt: [résumé] Marque américaine fondée en 1935 : guitares électriques, basses et amplis ; dormante après la fermeture de Valco, relancée en 2014

sources.title: Supro Solidbody Guitars - 1952 through 1967
sources.excerpt: By 1952 Valco began manufacturing solid body electric guitars under the National and Supro brand names.

sources.title: List of Vintage Supro Guitars, Basses and Amplifiers
sources.excerpt: Supro guitars were first produced in the 1930s by the National Dobro Corporation (rebranding as Valco in the 1940s)
